title: Put the organs back
subtitle: Ten organs are out of place
intro: Touch an organ with the pen, hold the button and carry it to the glowing outline where it belongs.

structures.name: Heart
structures.summary: A muscular pump about the size of a fist. It sits between the lungs, a little to the left, and sends blood round the body.
structures.fact: It beats about 100,000 times a day.

structures.name: Left lung
structures.summary: Smaller than the right lung, to leave room for the heart.
structures.fact: The left lung has two lobes; the right has three.

structures.name: Right lung
structures.summary: The larger lung. It sits on the right of the chest, with the liver just below it.
structures.fact: Together the lungs hold hundreds of millions of tiny air sacs.

structures.name: Liver
structures.summary: The largest organ inside the body. It lies on the right, under the ribs, and cleans the blood, makes bile and stores energy.
structures.fact: It can regrow after part of it is removed.

structures.name: Stomach
structures.summary: A stretchy bag on the left that mixes food with acid and starts to break it down.
structures.fact: An adult stomach can hold about a litre of food and drink.

structures.name: Spleen
structures.summary: A soft organ on the left, behind the stomach. It filters old blood cells and helps to fight infection.
structures.fact: It is about the size of a fist.

structures.name: Left kidney
structures.summary: One of two bean-shaped filters at the back, either side of the spine. It cleans the blood and makes urine.
structures.fact: Between them, the kidneys filter all of your blood many times a day.

structures.name: Right kidney
structures.summary: Its twin on the right. The liver pushes it a little lower than the left one.
structures.fact: You can live a healthy life with just one kidney.

structures.name: Small intestine
structures.summary: A long coiled tube where most of the food you eat is broken down and absorbed into the blood.
structures.fact: It is about six metres long, coiled up to fit.

structures.name: Large intestine
structures.summary: It frames the small intestine. It absorbs water and turns what is left into waste.
structures.fact: It is about one and a half metres long.
